why: The v1/v2 estimator (difference of within-week conditional rates, averaged over weeks) is biased toward reversal when the condition is built from the previous outcome (the 'hot hand' small-sample bias, Miller and Sanjurjo 2018): on independent coin flips it flags 'previous up' in 100 of 100 runs (validation.null_control). v3 uses the marginal rate difference with 28-day clustered standard errors (validation.marginal), which gives about zero on the same null.

v2's range outcome ('tomorrow's range above TODAY's') is close to circular for range conditions: a wide day is hard to beat by definition. v3 compares tomorrow's range with a normal day: the median of the 20 ranges up to today.
Exact complements (previous_down, momentum_5_down, momentum_20_down, narrow_range) answered the same question as their pairs and doubled the count; v3 keeps one of each pair.
estimator: validation.marginal: P(outcome | condition) - P(outcome | not condition); standard error clustered on 28-day blocks; normal interval at alpha / 128 (Bonferroni over every market x condition x outcome).

historical.status: seen before registration (v1, v2 and the validation page used this period): descriptive only, never evidence

prospective: Cumulative from 2026-12-01, recomputed each 1 December and frozen once computed. A result can be a candidate only when the cumulative prospective sample has at least 30 blocks (about 2.3 years, from late March 2029); earlier yearly snapshots are descriptive.
policy: Fixed plan; no parameter changes, no automatic promotion, no trading claim. A candidate means: worth a separately registered test with costs, not an edge. Known effects such as volatility clustering are expected to show up in the range outcome and are labelled as such.
